texts.preamble: M/S Sanjay Besan And Oil Mills Pvt. Ltd. ... vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Food And Drugs Admn ... on 19 December, 2019 Author: Z. A. Haq Bench: Z. A. Haq, M. G. Giratkar Judgment 1 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur. Criminal Application No. 3106/2009 1] M/ s. Sanjay Besan and Oil Mills (Private) Limited, Dubeyka Chowk, Mauranipur 284204 (Jhansi), Uttar Pradesh, through its Managing Director. 2] Harishankar Chintaman Seth, Managing Director, M/s. Sanjay Besan and Oil Mills (private) Limited, Dubeyka Chowk, Mauranipur 284204 (Jhansi), Uttar Pradesh, through its Managing Director. .... Petitioners // Versus // The State of Maharashtra, Through Food and Drugs Administration, Maharashtra State, Akola, at the instance of Food Inspector Shri Rambhau Gangaram Gawai. .... Respondent ______________________________________________________________ Shri P. R. Agrawal, Advocate for the applicants. Shri T. A. Mirza, A.P.P. for the non-applicant. _____________________________________________________________
texts.facts: 3] According to the complainant, Shri B. V. Kulkarni, Food Inspector had visited the premises of accused No.1 - Biharilal on 29 th August, 1994 and had drawn sample of Chana Dal and had sent it for analysis to the Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Amravati. According to the complainant, report of Public Analyst dated 10 th October, 1994 was received by the Food Inspector on 17 th October 1994, and as the report stated that Chana Dal was not of the standard as required by the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 Judgment 3 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt complaint came to be filed against the three accused, the accused No.1 - Biharilal being the seller and accused Nos.2 and 3 being the manufacturer. The complaint was filed on 07th August, 1997. 4] The applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) have approached this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying that the Reg.Cri.Case No.769/1997 registered against them before the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Various grounds are raised by the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3), one on it being that because of the delay in lodging the complaint, valuable right of the applicants conferred by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 is taken away. 5 ] On examining the submission made on behalf of the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) relying on the provisions of Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954, though we find that such submission would not have assisted the applicants in 1997 when the complaint came to be filed, as shelflife was not prescribed for the food article i.e. Chana Dal, however, now after 25 years of seizure of the food article, because of delay in service of summons on the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) and then because of pendency of this criminal application and the interim order granted by this Court, it is clear that the right conferred Judgment 4 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt on the accused by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954, is taken away. Hence, on this point itself the complaint filed against the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) has to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The officers who file the complaint before learned Magistrate, deliberately delay the filing of the complaint, and the complaint is filed just a couple of weeks before the expiry of shelflife of the seized articles and then the summons is served on the accused after the expiry of the shelflife of the seized articles and then the accused approaches this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure complaining that its valuable statutory right of getting the sample of seized article analyzed through Central or Public Laboratory is frustrated and this Court has no option but to quash the proceedings. It is noticed that this is the modus operandi of the accused and the officer filing the complaint and also the police officers entrusted with the job of serving summons/warrants on the accused.
